questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, should you back toward the driver's side?
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when possible. This gives you the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: When should you shift into a lower gear before going downhill?

options.text: As you begin to move downward
As you go downhill and pick up speed

questions.explanation: Slow down and shift into a lower gear before starting down a hill. If you don't, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that slows down a vehicle
A device that reduces engine noise
A device that improves fuel economy

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that slows down a vehicle
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow vehicles and reduce the need to use brakes.

questions.question: When drivers turn, which direction do they usually look?

options.text: In the direction of the turn
In the opposite direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: Drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. Body movements can show your intent to turn even if you don't signal.

questions.question: What should you not do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks
Change gears while on the tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes
A type of air brake system

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: How should you stop in an emergency?

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop
Veer your trailer to the left and stop

questions.explanation: Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight while still letting you turn if needed.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap, what should you check?

options.text: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin
questions.explanation: Make sure the fifth wheel locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin shaft, not around the kingpin head.

questions.question: What should a driver ensure about the truck's cargo?

options.text: The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer

questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safe vehicle operation. Improper loading can affect how the vehicle handles, damage the vehicle, and cause cargo to fall and injure people.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on your driving skills and how safely and responsibly you drive. You must obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. You must not cause an accident or break any traffic laws.

questions.question: If you drive through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.text: Try to stop in the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift into a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of your brake system.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must do all of the following except:
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat knowledge test, have a security check, prove you are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and have an FBI fingerprint check and criminal background check.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Keep a parked vehicle from moving.
Make it easier for a parked vehicle to roll.
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a parked vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use the parking brake, wheel chocks can hold a parked vehicle in place on a level surface.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Drive carefully when transporting hanging meat. This load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and swings as you drive, which affects how you control the vehicle.

questions.question: A cracked rim should be:

options.text: Moved to one of a pair of dual tires.

questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving for any damage. Do not use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel as hard as possible.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the gas and push in the clutch. This will help you regain traction.

questions.question: When driving, how can you stay alert?

options.text: Keep cool by using the air conditioner or opening a window.
Eat a lot of heavy foods.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cool by using the air conditioner or opening a window.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue while driving, keep the cab cool with the air conditioner or an open window. Avoid heavy foods and take rest breaks about every two hours or 100 miles.

questions.question: What color light means a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: On vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), a yellow light alerts you that the ABS is not working.

questions.question: Which is not a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. It is especially important to check them when turning, changing lanes, merging, and making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: How should you complete parallel parking on the driver's side?

options.text: Drive straight into the parking space.
Back up past the parking space, then drive forward into it.
Drive past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: When parallel parking, drive past the parking space first. Then back up carefully into the space. Keep your vehicle completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: What is a sign of standing water on the road?
questions.explanation: Tire splashes, clear reflections, and raindrops on the road all show standing water. Standing water can cause your tires to lose grip on the road.

questions.question: How should you park to make it easier to leave?

options.text: Park so you can back up when leaving.
Park so you can drive forward when leaving.
Park only on the side of roads, not in parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park so you can drive forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous. Try to park in a spot where you can drive forward when you leave.

questions.question: Is it important to watch what is behind your vehicle while driving?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder regularly. This helps you know what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Tired drivers cause more crashes at night than at any other time.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Drive onto the shoulder if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive onto the shoulder if needed.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may help you avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support heavy vehicles.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance away and recheck that all lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle?

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. You can also chock the wheels if needed for extra safety.

questions.question: In cold weather, when do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: After other parts of the road
Before other parts of the road
At the same time as other parts of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces in cold weather. Drive slowly and carefully on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: What is a problem with rough acceleration?

options.text: It helps you stay awake on long trips.
It can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and transmission. Always accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: If you will transport hazardous materials that require placards, you must:

options.text: Ask permission from local law enforcement.

questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport materials that require placards.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice anything that affects safety or could cause mechanical problems, you should:

options.text: Wait to see if the problem goes away.
Write about it in your vehicle report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write about it in your vehicle report.
questions.explanation: At the end of your driving shift, you may need to complete a written report about your vehicle. Always report anything that could affect safety or cause mechanical problems.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert while driving?
questions.explanation: Eating heavy foods or keeping the cab too warm can make you drowsy. Exercise and a healthy diet help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it may look wet instead of icy. Watch for black ice when roads look wet and temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: If a truck has one, a trailer brake hand valve is used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve can stop the truck from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if the vehicle has them.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, if you see no spray from other vehicles' tires, it means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from other tires means ice has formed on the road. Be very careful when driving in wet, freezing conditions.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens most often when:

options.text: A vehicle travels faster than 60 mph.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely with low tire pressure and worn tire tread on wet roads. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water.

questions.question: In hot weather, spots where tar is bleeding on the pavement:

options.text: Have the same traction as the rest of the road.
Have more traction than the rest of the road.

questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar rises to the road surface and becomes very slippery. Watch for these areas.

questions.question: When taking the driving test and asked to turn, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.

questions.explanation: When asked to turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake wear. The four basic types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: On all wheels of a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all wheels of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are on every wheel. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: How far will an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. At 55 mph under ideal conditions, an air brake vehicle needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, there is a problem in the system that needs to be fixed by a mechanic.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Reduce speed on surfaces with low traction. On packed snow, reduce speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. These must use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:
questions.explanation: Never overinflate tires. Always check tire pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: Skids happen when:

options.text: Tires lose grip on the road.
There is too much weight in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Skids occur when tires lose traction. Common causes are over-braking, over-accelerating, over-steering, and speeding.

questions.question: For a driving test:

options.text: You must provide the same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
You can use any vehicle, even if it is different from the type you will use with the CDL.
The testing station will provide the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must provide the same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
questions.explanation: The test must be taken in the type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing the test vehicle.
